facts.text: Heat Shield was deployed at Meridiani Planum during Opportunity (MER-B) in 2004.

Opportunity drove to examine its own heat shield, which had impacted the surface about 250 metres from the landing site. Near the heat shield, the rover found an iron-nickel meteorite, later named Heat Shield Rock — the first meteorite identified on another planet. It confirmed that the Martian atmosphere was once thicker.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Led to the discovery of Heat Shield Rock, the first meteorite identified on another planet — an iron-nickel meteorite that confirmed Mars's thinner atmosphere allows more impacts.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Meridiani Planum.
The crushed heat shield and nearby meteorite remain on the surface of Meridiani Planum, a pair of space-hardware and space-rock side by side.
